# osm-katana

Fast OpenStreetMap format converter — OSM **XML / BZ2 / GZ / PBF → GeoParquet / PBF**
with parallel decompression. A sub-crate of the
[znippy-zoomies](https://codeberg.org/nordisk/znippy-zoomies) workspace.

## CLI

```
osm-katana convert   <input>             # OSM XML/BZ2/GZ/PBF → GeoParquet
osm-katana convert   <input> --clip "min_lon,min_lat,max_lon,max_lat"  # bbox region clip
osm-katana convert   <input> --buildings # keep building=* footprints + heights/levels
osm-katana convert   <input> --vtd-workers 1   # single-worker (single-core lens)
osm-katana xml2pbf   <input> [output]    # OSM XML/BZ2 → PBF
osm-katana pbf2geo   <input>             # PBF → GeoParquet
osm-katana geo2arrow <input> <output>    # GeoParquet → Arrow IPC
osm-katana verify    [dir]               # inspect / verify GeoParquet output
```

## Library

The `osm_katana` crate exposes the same conversion as a library API (`convert()`),
run in-process on a worker pool — no subprocess, no shell-out. It reads compressed
input directly (the parallel `lbzip2` / `lgz` decompressors), so a `.osm.bz2` or
`.osm.pbf` is converted in one pass. The node prologue — mandatory sequential work on
a non-seekable `bz2` stream — is skipped with a **streaming, seek-free VTD** (see
[Streaming VTD](#streaming-vtd) below).

## Convert benchmarks

`osm-katana convert` (OSM XML → GeoParquet) head-to-head with the legacy single-stream
C++ reference tools `osmium` / `osmconvert` for the **same** input. One convert pass,
min-of-3. Columns: MB/s · cores busy · wall seconds · peak RSS (MB). The convert rows
share the workspace bench harness ([`../examples/nornir-bench.rs`](../examples/nornir-bench.rs))
and warehouse under `repo=znippy-zoomies`; the head-to-head also renders in that repo's
README under **OSM converter** ([`../README.md`](../README.md)).

### Multi core — all cores

`osm-katana` fans the convert across every core on a no-barrier gatling pipeline;
`osmium` / `osmconvert` are the single-stream C++ references (benched only when installed).

### Staged pipeline

The classic planet chain — each stage eats the **previous stage's output file**:
`xml2pbf` (OSM XML/bz2 → PBF) → `pbf2geo` (PBF → GeoParquet) → `geo2arrow` (GeoParquet →
Arrow IPC). `NORNIR_OSM_KATANA_CHAIN=1 nornir bench run znippy-zoomies` warehouses one row
per stage; point `NORNIR_OSM_KATANA_INPUT` at a planet for the heavy chain.

## Streaming VTD

The planet is `bz2` — a **non-seekable stream** — so the changesets + the whole node
prologue MUST be decompressed sequentially no matter what. `osm-katana`'s two-pass VTD
(`seek_past_nodes`) assumes a seekable mmap and re-seeks past the nodes, wasting that
mandatory leading decompression. The **single-pass** streaming VTD
([`znippy_zoomies::vtd_single_pass`](../src/vtd_single_pass.rs)) makes the mandatory pass
do double-duty: fed the decompressor's byte chunks in stream order (never a seek), it
scans and discards the node prologue and, the instant it crosses the node→way boundary,
flips to storing the `ElemIndex` for ways + relations — seek-free, O(1)-memory boundary
detection with a cross-chunk straddle carry. Byte-identical to the two-pass way/relation
subset (proven by unit tests). Opt-in; the full-planet FASTER-and-byte-identical compare
is deferred to the quiet bench box.
